body: Found and fully recovered live during S141-04 (registering the NORN agent). Root cause: cmd/bootstrap's writeSecretsEnv wrote var/agent-secrets.env by overwriting it with ONLY the current run's newly-provisioned secrets, not merging with what was already there. On any run that provisions at least one genuinely new agent (today: EDIS-WOOCOMMERCE, EMILY-TRAINING, EDIS-CUSTODIAN, NORN all needed provisioning for the first time - a separate, also-real bug where they'd been added to config/agents.json without ever being fully bootstrapped), this silently destroyed the plaintext for every agent NOT in that run's list. The database api_key_hash for EMILY-PRIME, FATBABY-EMILY, EMIREE, JON, BOB, and TYLER was untouched (those agents kept working via already-issued JWTs / already-running processes), but their plaintext secret vanished from the only place it is ever written - a git-ignored file with no backup by design, per the codebase's own security convention. Caught within the same work session, not after the fact: testing NORN's new Apple-filing capability end-to-end (emily apples post) failed immediately because EMILY-PRIME's own secret was gone. Recovery: EMILY-PRIME's plaintext was recoverable verbatim from a live running process's environment (/proc/<pid>/environ, the emily-agent daemon still had it loaded). The other five were not recoverable by any means found (confirmed via a full grep of the repo for hardcoded copies and a full /proc scan of every fatbaby-owned process for cached copies - nothing found) and were deliberately rotated: cleared their api_key_hash in the database directly, then ran bootstrap normally to regenerate fresh secrets for exactly those five. All ten agents (the original six plus the four newly registered) were then individually verified live against the running IDUNA instance - every single one authenticates successfully with its current secret. Fixed the root cause: writeSecretsEnv now parses and merges with any existing file content instead of overwriting, so this specific failure mode cannot recur. 6 new regression tests, including one that names the exact bug. Also found and fixed a related .gitignore bug while committing the test file: a bare 'bootstrap' pattern (meant only for the compiled binary at repo root) was shadowing the entire cmd/bootstrap/ source directory, silently hiding any new file added there from git - this could have hidden the regression test itself if not caught. No external exposure: these are M2M service credentials between components on the same machine, never transmitted anywhere except at the moment of use, and no evidence any consumer had cached the old values outside the recovered/verified set. Full detail: IDUNA CHANGELOG.md 2026-07-16, commit with the writeSecretsEnv fix.
title: Near-incident (fully recovered): bootstrap silently destroyed 6 agents' plaintext secrets
